question: azrikam-3 is recorded with more than one father: hashabiah, hashabiah-2.

actions.why: Both records represent Amaziah, son of Hilkiah and father of Hashabiah, in the same genealogy. The preceding verse identifies this as Ethan's Merarite line.
The Hebrew repeats the Shemaiah–Hasshub–Azrikam–Hashabiah chain of 1CH 9:14 and adds Bunni as Hashabiah's father. This identifies the target as the Hashabiah represented by hashabiah-11.

Azrikam's father in this chain is Hashabiah son of Bunni; neither passage identifies him with the son of Amaziah or the son of Jeduthun. Row 103663 already records the relationship using hashabiah-11.
Bunni is the father of the Hashabiah in Shemaiah's ancestry. This relationship belongs to hashabiah-11; 1CH 25:3 explicitly names Jeduthun as the father of the singer represented by hashabiah-2.
The Hebrew places son of Bunni immediately after Hashabiah in the ancestry of Shemaiah. The corresponding person record is hashabiah-11.
The Hebrew explicitly identifies this Hashabiah as son of Bunni.
The Shemaiah–Hasshub–Azrikam–Hashabiah genealogy is identified as belonging to the sons of Merari. This establishes clan descent, not direct fatherhood.

note: The repeated Hebrew genealogy identifies Azrikam's father with hashabiah-11; Hashabiah son of Amaziah also has independently supported Merarite descent in 1CH 6:44–45. Row 106044 is retained as an owner-instructed ruling, although 1CH 9:14 does not establish that its Hashabiah is Jeduthun's son.
